newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME hogs end strong on report expectations.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME hogs end strong on report expectations.

text.p: Expectations that Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs Report will be bullish to hog prices lifted nearby CME hog futures to new days highs in the closing range.

Traders cited scattered buying in nearbys late, especially February, on expectations the report could show total U.S. hog numbers and market hog numbers down from last year. Estimates for increased breeding numbers kept deferred months pressured, traders said.
February set its days high in the closing range before ending 0.650 higher at 76.750 cents.
Other months ranged from 0.525 cent higher to 0.225 lower.

Analysts estimates for All hogs as of December 1 averaged 98.4 percent of a year ago in a range of 95 to 101 percent. Hogs kept for breeding estimates averaged 101.6 in a range of 99.9 to 104 and kept for market estimates averaged 97.5 in a range of 94 to 99 percent.
In hog options, trade was thin with volatility unchanged. Commission houses were bidding on February 78 calls and offering 79 puts, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures retreated again in late trade as a midday recovery lacked followthrough and futures ran into resistance at Friday's closing level. Trading was very thin and commercial liquidation developed when support was lacking despite the strength in hog futures and a steady to firm tone to cash bellies at noon, traders said.
R.J. O'Brien sold after midday and ING notably sold late. Locals were on both sides of the market, pit sources said.
Pork bellies closed 0.225 to 0.850 cents lower with February off 0.375 at 77.950 cents.
